Let me preface this by saying I've never been a dog person. That said, I live in SE Austin, and there has always been one or two stray dogs that hang around the area, but lately my area has become more popular and I'm tired of it. Part of the reason is two of my immediate neighbors seem to encourage, feed, and socialize with the two long term strays, and now I'm noticing two more always around.

I like to let my cat come outside in my front yard while I smoke a cig, and she is a retarded inside cat and I've had a couple close calls where I've had to chase the dogs off my lawn to protect her. The dogs also scare some of the delivery drivers, and even bark at me from a distance. I've tried 311, no help... possibly because the dogs are near the neighbors when they come by, who knows....

I figured I would get better feedback from voaters than that other site. I know Austin is dog friendly and all, but strays running around with no tags for years on end is getting to me. Suggestions?
How to handle stray neighborhood dogs
side note, there is one dog I don't mind, he leaves my cat alone, and is the one of four that doesnt sit 10 feet outside my front door and bark all night.

First, try to determine if anyone owns the dog and nicely ask them to contain it. In my experience, most people are embarrassed their dog is bothering others, and genuinely did not know it was.

If the problem persists, trap the dog and call Animal Control.

An easy way to trap them is to purchase a dog carrier and put some food inside. When the dog goes inside, pull the door shut with a long string.

If you don't want that expense, a large cardboard box set up like a rabbit trap will work. Similar to this.

These dogs have been around for years now, at least two of them. Some come and go, right now there are two new dogs roaming with the pack, and they do have tags, but they are very aggressive so I'm not going anywhere near them. The two that have been around for a long while don't have tags, and run away if you get near, so trapping probably won't work. So for Animal control to come, I have to trap the dog(s) myself?
Sounds like you should call Animal Control and have them advise you.
Sounds like a plan since 311 didn't seem to work, thanks for the feedback

Have a long talk with your neighbor who is feeding these animals. Encourage them to formally adopt these dogs, get them checked by a vet, and take them into his or her home on a permanent basis. If they really cared they would have done this already. Explain politely that you are concerned for the dogs as there is a pack forming which could threaten the health and safety of both the dogs as well as neighborhood children and other folks pets.

There is also the option of trapping them and taking them to a no kill shelter for proper care. You could look up various animal rescue groups to see about borrowing a trap in exchange for a small donation or something.

Other people with this same problem told me about a third solution... but whether you choose to try this is solely up to you. Use a cheap pellet gun to discourage the dogs. Discretion is absolutely mandatory. Remove the screen from a window on your home so you can crack it open just enough to line up your shots. Don't go all Rambo, just a few quick shots here and there will suffice so the dogs learn to associate your area with getting popped in the butt with a stinging projectile. Paintballs from a paintball gun might work also for larger dogs. Please don't aim for the head! Only aim for the hind quarters or haunches so the ammo bounces off and leaves a good sting. I cannot stress enough how important it is to do this when no children or people are in the same vicinity as many Austin people freak out when they even think they see any kind of gun and you don't want anything to ricochet and hit somebody.
Thats the legality of a airsoft or pellet gun in city limits? I know Paintball guns can get you a ticket.

All 3 are legal to own in city limits. Unless you are shooting song birds, endangered species, old ladies, or breaking windows with them you are unlikely to have any problems. I only suggested the "shoot from inside" idea because it is hot outside and if someone were to drive by and see a rifle in your hand there is a chance they would get the wrong idea. Stick to the pellet gun, a pump action model from Wal-Mart works great on all manner of stray animals and unwanted critters. Pump action is ideal as you can increase the force of the pellet depending on the size or stubborness of the animal. Also with pump action there is no need to buy C02 cartridges so you save money.
